fluid-parcel.def: A small, imagined portion of a fluid treated as an object, so Newton's laws can be applied to it.

buoyant-force.def: The net upward force a fluid exerts on an object in it, because the pressure on the object's bottom is larger than on its top.

archimedes.def: The buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid the object displaces: F_b = ρ_fluid V_displaced g. It does not depend on the object's own density.

neutral-buoyancy.def: The condition in which the buoyant force on an object equals its weight, so it neither rises nor sinks. A fully submerged object is neutrally buoyant when its average density equals the fluid's; a floating object reaches the same balance with only part of it under the surface.
